PDF 77 line 14: one route is type-spec, defined by the locally owned R702.
PDF 77 line 14: the other route is declaration-type-spec, defined by the locally owned R703.

The premise is derived-type-spec inside R702, not every occurrence of derived-type-spec.

PDF 77 lines 20-29: the complete ten-alternative declaration-type-spec production.
PDF 77 line 20: bare intrinsic specifier.
PDF 77 line 21: TYPE wrapper around an intrinsic specifier.
PDF 77 line 22: TYPE wrapper around a derived specifier.
PDF 77 line 23: TYPE wrapper around an enum specifier.
PDF 77 line 24: TYPE wrapper around an enumeration specifier.
PDF 77 line 25: named derived CLASS form, subject to extensibility and entity attributes.
PDF 77 line 26: unlimited polymorphic CLASS(*) form.

PDF 77 lines 30-31.
The context is a declaration-type-spec, not every runtime type-spec.
Every ordinary type-param-value in the declaration is a specification expression, including named derived parameters.
A colon is excepted from this expression requirement; 7.2/C702 still requires POINTER or ALLOCATABLE.
An asterisk is excepted from this expression requirement; assumed-parameter contexts in 7.2, C726, and C7100 still apply.
PDF 77 lines 32-33.
Applies to derived-type-spec in a declaration-type-spec using the CLASS keyword; it does not restate C712 for CLASSOF.
7.5.7.1 excludes SEQUENCE, BIND, C_PTR and C_FUNPTR from extensibility; ABSTRACT alone does not exclude extensibility.
PDF 77 line 34.
The spelling TYPE(derived-type-spec) is decisive; CLASS(abstract-type) has a different premise.
An abstract type cannot be specified by this TYPE form, even if a POINTER or ALLOCATABLE attribute would avoid immediate instantiation.
PDF 77 line 35. The draft prints the association (R702); retain the official C707 identity and printed association without correcting it to R703.
The actual restriction explicitly names TYPE(intrinsic-type-spec), despite the printed R702 association.
The inner intrinsic specifier cannot end in a comma. R722's old character length syntax supplies a genuine otherwise-admitted trailing comma, with C729/C730 respected.
PDF 77 lines 36-37; two keywords and three alternative eligibility conditions.
The rule applies to entities declared with CLASS, including CLASS(*).
The rule also applies to entities declared with CLASSOF.
Being a dummy argument is sufficient for this constraint; POINTER or ALLOCATABLE is not additionally required.
Having ALLOCATABLE is an alternative eligibility condition, including for a function result when declared in a permitted statement.
Having POINTER is another alternative; it does not require simultaneous ALLOCATABLE.
PDF 77 lines 38-39: only two statement categories admit these specifiers.
TYPEOF is subject to the location restriction.
CLASSOF is independently subject to the location restriction.
A type declaration statement is an allowed location, including a properly attributed function-result declaration.
A component definition statement is the other allowed location; component restrictions remain dependencies.
Other declaration-type-spec contexts are excluded. The finite negatives use FUNCTION prefixes under R1530 rather than misusing R702 in ALLOCATE or SELECT TYPE.
PDF 77 lines 40-41.
The ordering rule applies to the TYPEOF data-ref.
The ordering rule also applies to the CLASSOF data-ref.
The referenced type must already be established; a later declaration under IMPLICIT NONE does not satisfy this premise.
All referenced type parameters must also be established. A parameter-only ordering negative remains explicitly pending, not silently equated to the forward-type case.
A previous declaration is one accepted route.
Establishment by the applicable implicit typing rules is the alternative route, including an explicitly mapped derived type for CLASSOF.
PDF 78, printed 64, line 1; TYPEOF-specific exclusions.
The TYPEOF data-ref cannot be unlimited polymorphic. TYPE(*) is also unlimited polymorphic by 7.3.2.2 p3; allocation to a concrete dynamic type does not change the prohibition.
The TYPEOF data-ref cannot have an abstract declared type, even when an allocated dynamic extension is concrete.
PDF 78 line 2; CLASSOF-specific exclusions.
An assumed-type data-ref is excluded. An ordinary CLASS(*) data-ref is not assumed-type and is explicitly handled by p3.

An intrinsic declared type is excluded. The text does not say 'only extensible derived type': enum, enumeration, and nonextensible nonintrinsic cases cannot be removed by inventing an extra condition.
PDF 78 lines 3-4.
The condition is that the data-ref has OPTIONAL, not that the newly declared entity is optional, and not that an optional argument happens to be present at runtime.
TYPEOF is one affected specifier.
CLASSOF is the other affected specifier.
An OPTIONAL data-ref cannot have a deferred parameter; removing OPTIONAL is a repair, not replacing the deferred oracle by a fixed length.
An OPTIONAL data-ref cannot have an assumed parameter; optional fixed-parameter controls remain admitted.
PDF 78 lines 5-7 names what each of the four kinds of specifier denotes. These are definitions of the alternatives, not duplicate S requirements or exhaustive type-interaction assertions.
PDF 78 line 5: an intrinsic specifier identifies its named intrinsic type and parameter values; detailed semantics stay in 7.4.
PDF 78 lines 5-6: a derived specifier identifies its named derived type and parameter values; detailed semantics stay in 7.5.
PDF 78 lines 6-7: an enum specifier identifies its named enum type; 7.6.1 defines this parameterless type.
PDF 78 line 7: an enumeration specifier identifies its named enumeration type; 7.6.2 defines this distinct parameterless type.
PDF 78 lines 8-12: observable declared-type, parameter, and polymorphism semantics of TYPEOF/CLASSOF.
PDF 78 line 8: the ordinary copying rule first applies when data-ref is not unlimited polymorphic; the final sentence supplies the CLASS(*) case.
PDF 78 lines 8-9: use the declared type, not the currently allocated or associated dynamic type.
PDF 78 lines 8-10: corresponding type parameter values are taken from data-ref; assumed values are values, not copied asterisks.
PDF 78 lines 9-10: a deferred parameter remains deferred instead of freezing its current allocated value.
PDF 78 lines 10-11: TYPEOF declares a nonpolymorphic entity.
PDF 78 line 10: CLASSOF declares a polymorphic entity.
PDF 78 lines 11-12: CLASSOF of CLASS(*) is equivalent to CLASS(*), not to the specifier for its current dynamic type.
Unnumbered source lines following p3 on PDF 78; this note describes contexts whose actual syntax and constraints remain in their defining clauses.
Array constructors, SELECT TYPE, and ALLOCATE use type-spec in the relevant productions. R1156's separate CLASS IS alternative uses derived-type-spec directly.
The note identifies integer-type-spec in DO CONCURRENT and FORALL; it does not transfer those statement grammars into this catalogue.
The note contrasts other uses of declaration-type-spec; C709 still limits TYPEOF/CLASSOF within that union.
Unnumbered source lines on PDF 78 explain p3, without imposing an independent diagnostic or duplicating its S requirement.
The declared entities' parameters depend on those of data-ref, as specified by p3.
Copying a data-ref's source declaration is not an implementation of TYPEOF/CLASSOF semantics.

An assumed parameter contributes its current value; newly declared entities, including dummy arguments, do not thereby acquire an assumed parameter. The character dummy sentinel probe tests the normative p3 effect.

requirements.title: Type-spec admits four type categories
requirements.definition: A type-spec is an intrinsic, derived, enum, or enumeration type specifier. The last two are distinct nonintrinsic types, not derived types. The union preserves the defining syntax, parameter conditions, and contextual restrictions of each alternative.
requirements.oracle: Four independent positive controls use an explicit type-spec in a small array constructor and check two initialized elements. Named enum values are constructed as enum values, not arbitrary integers without the required enumerator relationship.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Admission of each alternative is not proof of every type interaction or every enclosing context. No malformed defining alternative is misattributed to the union as an isolated R702 negative. Named enum/enumeration controls remain valid-source drafts if reference implementations lack them.
requirements.dependencies: 7.4.1/R704-R706 (PDF 80), 7.5.9/R754-R755 (PDF 106), 7.6.1/R764 and 7.6.2/R770 (PDF 109-112), 7.8/R777-R778/C7121-C7125/p3 (PDF 114-115). 4.1.2 and 4.2 p2(3) (PDF 45-46) supplies the numbered-syntax reporting basis, not mandatory fatal rejection.

requirements.title: Declaration-type-spec has ten alternatives
requirements.definition: The declaration category admits a bare intrinsic specifier; TYPE around an intrinsic, derived, enum, or enumeration specifier; CLASS around a derived specifier; CLASS(*); TYPE(*); and TYPEOF or CLASSOF applied to a data-ref. TYPE(*) is assumed-type; CLASS(*) is unlimited polymorphic. TYPEOF/CLASSOF do not accept an arbitrary expression merely because it has a type.
requirements.oracle: Ten separately compiled admission controls exercise the ten alternatives. The assumed-type object is a scalar INTENT(IN) dummy in an internal procedure and is used only by PRESENT; polymorphic objects have suitable attributes and are allocated or associated before value access.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These are positive controls for the union. They do not prove all type identity, dynamic type, parameter propagation, interoperability, or argument association effects. In particular the TYPE(*) control does not inspect its value or claim a C ABI result. TYPEOF/CLASSOF semantic evidence is separately owned by S7.3.2.1-001.
requirements.dependencies: 8.2/R801 (PDF 117); 7.3.2.2 p2-p3/C714-C716 (PDF 78), 7.3.2.3 and 7.3.3 (PDF 79); local C704-C713; defining type alternatives in 7.4-7.6. 15.4.2.1-15.4.2.2 (PDF 325) supplies explicit internal interfaces. Numbered syntax has the 4.2 p2(3) reporting basis.

requirements.title: R702 derived type-spec cannot be abstract
requirements.definition: A derived-type-spec used as the derived alternative of R702 cannot name an abstract type. The association with R702 is part of the premise. It does not prohibit CLASS(abstract-type) declarations or a CLASS IS(abstract-type) guard, whose derived-type-spec does not pass through R702.
requirements.oracle: A located compile-report fixture allocates an abstract type through a properly declared polymorphic allocatable. Its minimally repaired control substitutes a concrete extension in the allocation. A separate initialized CLASS IS guard control shows the R1156 boundary without calling it an abstract TYPE IS case.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No abstract constructor is used: that would add an independent violation. The allocation has an explicit compatible type-spec, scalar object, and correct attribute. A report must be at the allocation, not at a type definition or recovery summary. Required means detection/reporting capability under 4.2 p2(3), not a compulsory fatal exit.

requirements.title: Ordinary declaration parameter values are specification expressions
requirements.definition: In a declaration-type-spec, each type-param-value other than colon or asterisk must be a specification expression. This applies to positional and named parameters, intrinsic and derived. Specification expressions are not universally constant expressions: the context and restricted-expression rules matter. The colon and asterisk exceptions here do not waive their separate attribute and context restrictions.
requirements.oracle: Controls use supported KIND inquiries, a nonoptional INTENT(IN) scalar length dummy, legal assumed/deferred character contexts, and a PDT with named kind/length parameters. The isolated negative changes that length dummy to OPTIONAL; removing OPTIONAL is the repair. The diagnostic is bound to the character declaration.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The negative uses a scalar integer length, not a nonconstant kind (which would independently violate C701/R706) or an unsupported kind. The optional dummy's value is excluded by the restricted-expression definition regardless of runtime presence. No diagnostic requirement is inferred from arbitrary prose: the owned numbered C704 invokes the specification-expression definition.
requirements.dependencies: 7.2/R701-C702 (PDF 76); 10.1.11 p1-p4/R1029/C1011, especially p2(2) (PDF 185-186); 7.4.4.2/R721-R723/C726 (PDF 84-85); 7.5.3 and 7.5.9 (PDF 91-93,106). 4.1.2/4.2 gives required reporting rather than required refusal to compile.

requirements.title: CLASS named derived types must be extensible
requirements.definition: When a declaration-type-spec uses CLASS with a derived-type-spec, that type must be extensible. Under 7.5.7.1, SEQUENCE and BIND types and the intrinsic-module types C_PTR and C_FUNPTR are excluded. An abstract derived type can be extensible and is not banned by this condition. The text names the CLASS keyword, not CLASSOF.
requirements.oracle: Four independent located negatives use SEQUENCE, BIND(C), C_PTR, and C_FUNPTR with otherwise eligible POINTER declarations. Repairs remove SEQUENCE/BIND(C) or replace CLASS by TYPE for the intrinsic-module types. An abstract-extensible control allocates a concrete extension and checks initialized data.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No kind representation is hard-coded: BIND(C) uses C_INT. Pointer controls begin disassociated; no undefined pointer value or abstract dynamic object is read. These exclusions are a finite test of the exact extensibility definition, not an inherited ban on every CLASSOF operand. Diagnostics must identify the declaration, not an unsupported USE or type definition.
requirements.dependencies: 7.5.7.1 p1/p4 (PDF 104), 7.3.2.3/7.3.3 (PDF 79), 18.2 ISO_C_BINDING types/constants, and 4.1.2/4.2 p2(3). C708 supplies the independently satisfied POINTER/ALLOCATABLE premise.

requirements.title: TYPE with a derived specifier cannot name an abstract type
requirements.definition: TYPE(derived-type-spec) cannot specify an abstract type. This is a declaration restriction, distinct from the R702 type-spec restriction C703 and the TYPEOF operand restriction C711. Adding POINTER or ALLOCATABLE does not exempt this TYPE form; using CLASS is a different form with its own conditions.
requirements.oracle: The negative declares a TYPE object of a previously defined abstract type. The repaired control removes only ABSTRACT from the type definition, initializes a small component, and checks it. Report the object declaration, not the ABSTRACT type definition.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No deferred type-bound procedure, missing binding, constructor, or invalid type ordering is involved. The control is admission of the repaired TYPE declaration, not evidence that abstract CLASS entities are forbidden. The reporting contract does not require fatal rejection.

requirements.title: TYPE-wrapped intrinsic specifiers cannot end in a comma
requirements.source: 7.3.2.1 C707, printed association (R702); PDF 77, printed 63, line 35.
requirements.definition: In the explicitly named TYPE(intrinsic-type-spec) form, the inner intrinsic-type-spec must not end with a comma. Preserve the draft's printed R702 association without silently changing the official rule identity or ignoring its explicit TYPE-wrapper wording.
requirements.oracle: The negative uses TYPE(CHARACTER*3,) word, without a double-colon separator. Deleting the inner comma is the minimal repair. A separately compiled program with an unwrapped CHARACTER*3, word declaration shows that R722 really supplies an optional comma in an otherwise allowed declaration context; unsupported unwrapped syntax cannot mask the repaired TYPE control.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A trailing comma after INTEGER or inside KIND selectors would invent a separate syntax defect. A double colon would independently violate C730, so neither negative nor repair has one. The diagnostic point is the wrapped declaration; there is no required fatal status.
requirements.dependencies: 7.4.4.2/R721-R723 and C729-C730 (PDF 84-85); 8.2/R801 (PDF 117); 4.1.2 and 4.2 p2(3). The old character length form's spelling is a dependency, not newly owned R722 coverage.

requirements.title: CLASS and CLASSOF entities need one eligibility condition
requirements.definition: An entity declared using CLASS or CLASSOF must be a dummy argument or have ALLOCATABLE or POINTER. These are alternatives, not cumulative requirements. A function result is not a dummy argument merely because it belongs to a procedure; it needs the appropriate attribute. The operand of CLASSOF does not confer attributes on the new entity.
requirements.oracle: Separate CLASS and CLASSOF controls exercise dummy, allocated allocatable, and associated pointer forms with an explicit internal interface. Two declaration-only negative programs have an ordinary nondummy local without either attribute; the minimal repair adds ALLOCATABLE and never reads the unallocated object.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The bare-local negatives do not add ALLOCATE or ALLOCATED calls that would independently require the missing attribute. The repaired empty programs are positive admission evidence, not runtime type effects. Required reporting is from the numbered constraint under 4.2, not a fatal-exit policy.
requirements.dependencies: 7.3.2.3, 8.5 attributes, 15.4.2.1-15.4.2.2 (PDF 325), and 15.6.2.2 p3 (PDF 354). C705, C709-C713 are independently satisfied in each relevant control or negative.

requirements.title: TYPEOF and CLASSOF have two allowed statement locations
requirements.definition: A TYPEOF or CLASSOF specifier may occur only in a type declaration statement or a component definition statement. Membership in R703 does not admit these alternatives in every context accepting declaration-type-spec, such as a FUNCTION prefix, IMPLICIT mapping, or procedure interface specification.
requirements.oracle: Controls place each keyword in a function-result type declaration and in component definitions. Negatives put the same specifier in a FUNCTION prefix, an R1530 declaration-type-spec context. The repairs move the specifier into the result declaration. CLASSOF results/components have ALLOCATABLE, and all returned or read values are initialized.
requirements.oracle_limitation: ALLOCATE(TYPEOF(...)) and TYPE IS(TYPEOF(...)) would instead misuse R702; they are not C709 isolates. This finite packet does not enumerate every forbidden R703 context. Prefix diagnostics with only unsupported-feature or recovery evidence cannot corroborate the semantic restriction; retain the repaired control outcome and complete diagnostic.

requirements.title: TYPEOF and CLASSOF require established type information
requirements.definition: The data-ref operand of TYPEOF or CLASSOF must have both its type and its type parameters previously declared or established by the applicable implicit typing rules. A subsequent declaration under IMPLICIT NONE is not equivalent to prior establishment. Explicit declaration is not the only admitted route.

pending.parameter-only-ordering: A separate negative with established type but not-yet-established parameters has not been isolated without also violating the referenced object's own declaration rules. The prior kind/length controls and missing-prior-type negatives do not close this facet. Next evidence: source-review an independently invalid parameter-order data-ref, then bind its diagnostic and minimal repair.

requirements.oracle: Two negatives use a later-declared data-ref under IMPLICIT NONE; their repairs move the complete declaration before the specifier. Controls also exercise implicit default-integer establishment for TYPEOF and an explicit implicit-derived-type mapping for CLASSOF. Prior character and PDT declarations carry known type parameters.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This does not read an uninitialized value: the type information is established before any effect probe. Implicit CLASSOF uses a host-defined extensible derived type, not the default intrinsic implicit type that C712 excludes. The parameter-only negative is pending, not inferred from admission or from an unrelated later redeclaration error.
requirements.dependencies: 8.7/R866-R867/p3-p4 (PDF 141-142), 7.5.3/7.5.9 (PDF 91-93,106), and local C711-C713. 4.1.2/4.2 p2(3) gives the reporting obligation; 10.1.11 (PDF 185-186) remains a separate specification-expression dependency.

requirements.title: TYPEOF excludes unlimited polymorphic and abstract operands
requirements.definition: The data-ref in TYPEOF cannot be unlimited polymorphic or of abstract declared type. A concrete dynamic allocation does not supply a permitted substitute for the declared type. Assumed-type entities are also unlimited polymorphic under 7.3.2.2 p3. The restriction is on TYPEOF, not on CLASSOF.
requirements.oracle: Separate negatives apply TYPEOF to a previously declared CLASS(*) allocatable and to a CLASS(abstract-root) allocatable. Minimal declaration-only controls use CLASS(concrete-root) or remove ABSTRACT. Each report must identify TYPEOF, not the legal polymorphic operand declaration.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No value, deferred parameter, or allocation status is read by these declaration-only isolates. S7.3.2.1-001 separately distinguishes declared from dynamic type. No additional negative is attributed to C711 for an unrelated inaccessible or undefined type. A mere unsupported TYPEOF parser failure is not semantic corroboration.

requirements.title: CLASSOF excludes assumed-type and intrinsic operands
requirements.definition: The data-ref operand of CLASSOF cannot be assumed-type or of intrinsic declared type. CLASS(*) is not assumed-type and is explicitly admitted by p3. This constraint does not restrict operands to extensible derived types: C705 applies to a different keyword/premise, while named enum and enumeration types are nonintrinsic and are not derived types.
requirements.oracle: Located negatives use an otherwise legal TYPE(*) dummy and a previously declared integer. Repairs change the dummy to CLASS(*) or the integer to a defined derived type. Separate admission controls retain CLASSOF of a SEQUENCE object, a named enum object, and an enumeration object rather than weakening the source to match implementation support.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The assumed-type dummy has no prohibited attributes and is not executed or used in an unrelated expression. The CLASSOF occurrence is the explicit owned forbidden use. Nonextensible and enum controls claim declaration admission only, not extension, SELECT TYPE, C interoperability, or runtime representation. Unsupported controls remain source-only candidates pending independent review.

requirements.title: Optional TYPEOF and CLASSOF operands need nonassumed nondeferred parameters
requirements.definition: If the TYPEOF or CLASSOF data-ref has OPTIONAL, none of its type parameters may be deferred or assumed. The condition is on the operand, not on the newly declared entity. Presence at runtime does not waive this static restriction. Fixed parameters on an OPTIONAL operand and assumed/deferred parameters on a nonoptional operand do not violate this constraint.
requirements.oracle: Four isolated negatives cross the two keywords only with the two forbidden parameter categories: character for TYPEOF, a one-length PDT for CLASSOF. Each minimally repaired control removes OPTIONAL. Two additional fixed-parameter optional controls execute with the operand both present and absent, guarding any actual value reference with PRESENT.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The deferred declarations carry ALLOCATABLE and assumed parameters occur only on proper dummies. No intrinsic operand is passed to CLASSOF; all PDTs are defined before use. Declaration-only repaired controls are admission evidence, not a claim about parameter values. The reporting point is the TYPEOF/CLASSOF declaration and its message must concern OPTIONAL.

requirements.title: TYPEOF and CLASSOF preserve declared type and parameter semantics
requirements.source: 7.3.2.1 p3; PDF 78, printed 64, lines 8-12. Note 2 explains, but does not separately mandate, the assumed-parameter distinction.
requirements.definition: For a data-ref that is not unlimited polymorphic, TYPEOF and CLASSOF specify its declared type and corresponding type parameter values, not its current dynamic type. The exception is that a parameter deferred in data-ref remains deferred. TYPEOF declares a nonpolymorphic entity and CLASSOF a polymorphic entity. CLASSOF of a CLASS(*) data-ref is equivalent to CLASS(*). Assumed parameters supply their values rather than making the new entity assumed, including when that entity is itself a dummy argument.
requirements.oracle: Independent runtime programs distinguish a declared root from a dynamic extension; test a polymorphic result's ability to allocate sibling extensions; compare supported intrinsic kinds and explicit lengths; use a character dummy with a longer actual and untouched trailing sentinels to distinguish copied values from a copied asterisk; check named PDT kind/assumed-length values; allocate deferred character/PDT copies with lengths different from the source; and allocate a CLASSOF(CLASS(*)) result to types unrelated to its operand's current dynamic type. A component/array data-ref control checks type/parameters without inheriting rank.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is finite effect evidence, not every combination of type category, kind, rank, component path, pointer association, or optional attribute. All allocations/associations and sizes are checked before value or deferred-parameter access. Zero-sized arrays, coarrays, processor source interfaces, C ABI representation, and full enum TYPEOF/CLASSOF runtime interactions are outside this finite plan. Unsupported F2023 syntax, PDT lowering failures, crashes, and reference F2018 mode do not invalidate a source-valid oracle and do not count as effects. No negative or fatal diagnostic is inferred from this prose paragraph.
requirements.dependencies: 7.3.2.2-7.3.3 (PDF 78-79); 7.2 (PDF 76); 7.4.4.2 (PDF 84-85); 7.5.3/7.5.9 (PDF 91-93,106); 9.4.5 p2 (PDF 153); 9.7.1.1 (PDF 160-161); 11.1.11 (PDF 224-226); 15.4.2.2 (PDF 325); 15.5.2.5 p3-p5 (PDF 340) permits a scalar default-character actual longer than its fixed-length dummy. 16.9.118/KIND (PDF 424) supplies portable kind inquiries, and 16.9.171/RANK (PDF 449) checks the scalar receiving declaration. The execution interpretation is required by 4.2 p2(1), not an extra reporting obligation.

review_rationale: Independent original-source review and verified gate repairs: doc/source_audits/batch_007.json. R702/R703, C703-C713 and TYPEOF/CLASSOF propagation preserve the actual F2023 type, rank, parameter and polymorphism premises. C710's parameter-only ordering isolation remains pending. Unsupported reflection parsing is not a semantic diagnostic or an executed effect.
